# Browser-Native Search Agent — Architecture Spec

**Status:** DESIGN PROPOSAL — WRITTEN, NOT YET EXECUTED.
**Provenance:** Generated by Hermes session 2026-06-17 in response to master prompt
"Browser-Native Search Agent". All code in this document is illustrative; nothing here
has been compiled, run against a real browser, or wired into the AEGIS runtime.
**Static verification:** `wc -l` + `sha256sum` recorded in section Provenance.

---

## 0. Executive Summary

This spec proposes a 3-pillar architecture for deep-research over the live web:

1. **Browser Control Layer** (Python + Playwright) drives a real Chromium so we
   get JS rendering, anti-detection, and visual context.
2. **Search Quality Pipeline** (Perplexity-SaC style) multi-engine query,
   dedup, citation tracking.
3. **Cryptographic Verification** (AEGIS core) every browser action is sealed
   into a `BrowserObservationPacket` whose hash rides the same BLAKE3 chain as
   the rest of the system.

The proposal deliberately avoids inventing new JSON shapes where AEGIS already
has matching primitives. The prompt's `BrowserActionCapsule`, `BrowserActionType`,
and `BrowserIntegrationLayer` sketches are re-cast in section 3 as thin wrappers over
`core/rust/src/browser_witness.rs` types so we do not fork the on-disk schema.

Nothing in sections 3-6 has been implemented. Sections 1 and 2 are domain analysis based
on the prompt text alone, marked UNVERIFIED where claims are not anchored to
file:line in the existing tree.

UNVERIFIED claims (no live browser run, no Perplexity scrape in this session):
- Perplexity SaC citation format (CSS classes, hover behaviour)
- Live captcha / anti-bot response profiles for Google / Bing / DDG
- Whether 20 sample queries parity benchmark is achievable on the host

## 1. Why Browser-First (UNVERIFIED beyond prompt text)

Per the master prompt framing, every benefit listed is asserted by the prompt,
not independently measured. The architectural win is real (Playwright executes
the same JS a human user would; HTTP scrapers must reverse-engineer), but the
specific claims about Perplexity robustness are taken on faith until section 2 is
filled in by an actual Perplexity scrape.

| Concern                          | HTTP-first scrapers (4 repos)  | Browser-first (this design) |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| Real-time web access             | partial                        | yes (Playwright goto)       |
| JS-heavy sites                   | needs headless HTML parser     | yes (Chromium renders)      |
| Anti-detection                   | IP/UA ban surface              | harder to fingerprint       |
| Rich interaction (click/fill)    | yes but stateless              | yes with state              |
| Visual evidence                  | none                           | screenshot + DOM snapshot   |

## 3. Design, Reuse Existing AEGIS Types

The prompt sketches fresh `BrowserActionCapsule`, `BrowserActionType` and
`BrowserIntegrationLayer` types. AEGIS already has prior art in
`core/rust/src/browser_witness.rs`. Per the No Over-Engineering guardrail,
we wrap rather than duplicate.


All four 'every record carries `browser_session_hash: [u8; 32]`' rows
(browser_witness.rs lines 102, 123, 154, 209) confirm BLAKE3 session chaining
is already standard; we do not invent a separate hash registry.

### 3.2 Prompt `BrowserActionType` to existing `BrowserActionKind`

The prompt sketch lists 6 variants: Navigate(String), Click(String),
Fill(String,String), Screenshot(bool), Evaluate(String), WaitFor(String).
AEGIS `BrowserActionKind` (line 19) covers the first two with no payload and
the others through side artefacts: `TypeText` for `Fill`, `FindElements` for
selector probes, and the artifact kind enum (line 64) for screenshot / DOM snapshots.
Recommended mapping (PROPOSED, NOT YET COMPILED):

| Prompt sketch              | AEGIS binding                                  |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Navigate(url)              | BrowserActionKind::Navigate + plan.target      |
| Click(selector)            | BrowserActionKind::Click + plan.target         |
| Fill(selector, value)      | BrowserActionKind::TypeText + plan.target      |
| Screenshot(full)           | BrowserArtifactKind::Screenshot attached       |
| Evaluate(js)               | taken over by the live collector               |
| WaitFor(sel-or-timeout)    | derived from BrowserActionPlanKind only        |

When wired, the prompt `BrowserActionCapsule` becomes a thin helper that
emits a `BrowserActionTrace` plus `BrowserWitnessProof` pair through
`evidence_index::browser_page_search_candidate_record_hash`. It does NOT
become a top-level Rust module.

### 3.3 Prompt `BrowserIntegrationLayer` to existing ledger or learning modules

The prompt sketches a `BrowserIntegrationLayer { ledger, gate, search_index }`.
Looking at the tree:

```
core/rust/src/learning/mod.rs                       (LearningLedger)
core/rust/src/context.rs                            (CandidateOnlyGate)
core/rust/src/memory/session_search.rs              (SessionSearchIndex or HotLexicalIndex)
core/rust/src/memory/nudge.rs                       (MemoryNudgeSystem)
core/rust/src/memory/mod.rs
core/rust/src/evidence_index.rs                     (browser_page_search_*_hash)
```

Therefore the Python bridge in section 4 MUST import these modules by path; it MUST
NOT build a parallel `LearningLedger`. The PyO3 surface that should be added
is the smallest set that lets Python say:

- register a browser session: `LearningLedger::next_session_id`
- append a `BrowserObservationPacket`: `browser_witness::record`
- filter candidates through `CandidateOnlyGate`: existing gate function
- index a context pack into `SessionSearchIndex`: existing index fn
- search past sessions: existing FTS5 query

## 4. Python Bridge (ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT IMPLEMENTED)

The prompt code in `core/python/browser_agent.py` is reproduced below as
pseudocode so a future implementer can copy it verbatim; nothing here
is on disk yet. Imports reference the modules named in section 3.3. The named
exception `AegisBridge` does not exist today and would need to be authored
alongside `core/rust/src/browser_bridge.rs`.

```python
# ILLUSTRATIVE: WRITTEN, NOT YET EXECUTED
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright, Page
from aegis_bridge import AegisBridge, BrowserActionKind    # proposed names

class BrowserAgent:
    # Pseudocode skeleton. See section 3.2 for the AEGIS-type mapping.

    def __init__(self, bridge: AegisBridge):
        self.bridge = bridge
        self.playwright = None
        self.browser = None
        self.page = None          # type: Page | None
        self.session_id = None    # type: int | None

    async def start_session(self):
        self.playwright = await async_playwright().start()
        self.browser = await self.playwright.chromium.launch(
            headless=False,
            args=['--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled'],
        )
        context = await self.browser.new_context(
            user_agent='Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; ...',
        )
        self.page = await context.new_page()
        await self._apply_stealth(self.page)
        self.session_id = self.bridge.register_browser_session()

    async def navigate(self, url: str):
        sb = await self.page.screenshot()
        db = await self.page.accessibility.snapshot()
        await self.page.goto(url, wait_until='networkidle')
        sa = await self.page.screenshot()
        da = await self.page.accessibility.snapshot()
        capsule = self.bridge.record_observation(
            session_id=self.session_id,
            kind=BrowserActionKind.Navigate,
            target=url,
            screenshot=(sb, sa), dom=(db, da),
        )
        assert self.bridge.candidate_gate.validate(capsule)
        return capsule

    # --- search/verify methods identical to prompt (illustrative) ---
    def _compute_groundedness(self, content, claim):
        cw = set(claim.lower().split())
        bw = set(content.lower().split())
        return len(cw & bw) / max(len(cw), 1)
```

The `_apply_stealth` JS in the prompt is minimal and would need replacement
with `playwright-stealth` in production; calling it out so reviewers don't
ship the two-line stub verbatim.

## 6. Open Risks (Identified, Not Mitigated)

| Risk                                        | Probability | Impact   | Mitigation (PLANNED, not done)                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Perplexity rate-limits or bot detection     | Med         | Med      | Backoff + human-in-the-loop switch                  |
| Legal exposure (Google ToS)                 | Med         | High     | Treat as research tool; cite robots.txt             |
| Browser fingerprint drift                  | Low         | Med      | Pin to a known user-agent; rotate conservatively    |
| Schema drift from inventing parallel types  | Med         | High     | Reuse existing types per section 3.2                 |
| Replay determinism across sessions          | Med         | Med      | Lean on existing `browser_session_hash` chain       |
| 20-query benchmark not reachable under 30 min | High      | Low      | Cap scope to a smaller fixture (5-query smoke)      |
